title: [v0.4.31] Release: final semantic acceptance
author: mcpdev80
body:
## Aktuelle Grenze — v0.4.31

Reine abschließende semantische und sicherheitsbezogene Abnahme der zuvor gelieferten Basis. TLS-/Proxy-Umbauten #902 und Angriffsschutz #903 werden in **v0.4.30/#904** implementiert/qualifiziert und hier nur abschließend geprüft. Keine neue große Feature-/Provider-Entwicklung in dieser Abnahme; entdeckte echte Fehler müssen vor Freigabe korrigiert werden.

Abhängigkeit: qualifizierte vorherige Releases einschließlich #904. Danach no-new-features Stability-Reconciliation und #175/v0.5-Freeze. Ab v0.4.26 gilt #888 mit eigenen kleinen Task-PRs und verifizierter Evidence-Wiederverwendung; ältere Session-/Shared-Branch-Angaben unten sind historische Planung und nicht der aktuelle Arbeitsmodus.

## v0.4.31 — Final Semantic Acceptance (superseding former v0.4.25 release schedule)

## Authoritative v0.4.25–v0.4.31 release split (2026-10-10)
This schedule supersedes older 0.4.25-only and three-session plans wherever they conflict. Exactly **two development sessions per release**, distinct file ownership/PRs, a common exact-SHA integration gate, lean atomic tests first and target-specific runtime proof. Each release is individually completed, qualified and promoted before its successor. `#865–#871` remain assigned to **v0.4.24** and are not deferred.

| Release | Umbrella | Session 1 | Session 2 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| v0.4.25 | #872 | Contract, canonical minimal/shorthand, profile format | Core-less, dependency/footprint resolver, provider reuse |
| v0.4.26 | #873 | Greenfield/edit TUI and confirmation | CLI/JSON/MCP footprints and developer docs |
| v0.4.27 | #874 | Node Connector, remote/Core/Target authority | #777 onboarding, portable profile and access |
| v0.4.28 | #875 | Console API/management integration | Console UX, full developer journeys |
| v0.4.29 | #876 | #819/#820/#821 Host seam, Linux, WSL2 | #822 Darwin/macOS, #823 conformance, #817 audit |
| v0.4.30 | #904 | Native TLS / proxy simplification #902 | Attack protection baseline / DDoS boundaries #903 |
| v0.4.31 | #174 | Semantic/architecture/contract/security acceptance | #862 quality + final evidence/docs and freeze readiness |

Contract-semantic boundaries for later releases MUST be explicitly specified and pinned in **v0.4.25**, including #810's management Core vs core-less Application distinction, canonical shorthand and stable ID, footprint v1 and Target provider-state ownership, #777 profile import/export, Host Platform seams, and machine-interface parity. Later releases consume these contracts and may fix behavior/implementation bugs without quietly redefining them. Formal compatibility freeze remains #175/v0.5, not v0.4.25.

Quality, safety, ownership, CLI/JSON/MCP parity, documentation, and exact-SHA scoped evidence are per-release requirements, not first introduced in v0.4.31. #862's static/vulnerability gates should be introduced as early as practical, then ratcheted across each release; final review is part of #174. The Console AI-assistant boundary must be explicitly decided before #175; no stealth deletion or unproven claim.

**Release-only stability cycle:** after v0.4.31 qualification and before #175, perform a dedicated no-new-features reconciliation of contract, release evidence, independent developer journeys, docs, compatibility/security and outstanding defects. No tagging/freeze until evidence and scope agree.

**Roadmap hygiene:** #155 is the master roadmap, #427 tracks productization, each #872–#876 owns its focused delivery, #174 is FINAL semantic acceptance in v0.4.31, and #175 owns v0.5 formal freeze. Parent references #777, #817–#823 and #862 follow this schedule. Older planning sections are historical and non-normative.

---

## Goal

Close v0.4 by proving that BaseHarbor's language and lifecycle semantics are runtime-independent while Compose remains the complete reference runtime.

This release adds no new major capability and no Kubernetes implementation.

> **Developer experience first.**
>
> **Simple by default. Secure by default. Explicit when needed.**
>
> **As little as possible, as much as necessary.**

## Runtime boundary acceptance

BaseHarbor must clearly distinguish:

### Portable application state

Examples:

- stable application identity;
- logical capability requirements;
- logical resources;
- endpoint/exposure intent;
- secure-binding requirements;
- application-owned health/security requirements.

### Deployment/operator state

Examples:

- environment selection;
- runtime selection;
- capability-provider selection;
- provider placement;
- sharing boundaries;
- policy overrides.

### Runtime-owned realization state

Current Compose examples:

- Compose project names;
- generated overrides;
- host-port assignments;
- Docker/Podman network/container details;
- local runtime file paths.

Future examples such as Kubernetes namespaces, resource names, Services or PVCs remain runtime realization and must not require portable-contract changes.

### Provider-owned state

Examples:

- physical bucket/database identities;
- provider credentials;
- topology/product-specific configuration;
- provider lifecycle metadata.

### Generated/protected state

Generated credentials, fingerprints, runtime identity and other internal state remain outside repository-owned portable intent.

## Runtime-provider architecture rule

Capability providers and runtime providers are separate axes.

```text
                 BaseHarbor Core
                  /          \
                 /            \
        Runtime Provider    Capability Provider
              |                    |
           Compose              SQL / S3 /
        future Kubernetes      secrets / etc.
```

v0.4 only proves the boundary and current Compose implementation. A future Kubernetes runtime must be able to consume the same core semantics without redefining application intent.

Do not add a speculative runtime-provider framework beyond what the current Compose path and the documented future boundary demonstrably require.

## Reference journeys

Human journey:

```text
inspect
  ↓
app init / adopt
  ↓
plan
  ↓
up/apply
  ↓
status
  ↓
doctor
  ↓
update
  ↓
backup
  ↓
restore
  ↓
drift / repair
  ↓
destroy
```

Agent/machine journey:

```text
discover
  ↓
inspect
  ↓
plan
  ↓
policy
  ↓
safe mutation
  ↓
status / doctor
  ↓
verification / evidence
```

## Semantic acceptance

Prove that:

- CLI, JSON and MCP use the same underlying state/result semantics;
- runtime-specific names/details never become application identity;
- provider placement can change without rewriting application intent;
- Compose realization remains behind a runtime boundary;
- status/doctor/policy/evidence agree on actual state;
- provider/runtimes report capability readiness through real verification;
- lifecycle operations preserve ownership and isolation;
- later-runtime concepts have not leaked into the v0.4 portable contract.

## Developer-experience acceptance

- five-minute local journey remains valid;
- normal configuration stays sparse;
- BaseHarbor explains inferred/resolved state without dumping provider noise;
- dangerous ambiguity fails closed with actionable guidance;
- no security questionnaire;
- no new knob is added unless a demonstrated use case needs it;
- product terminology is consistent;
- current behavior is documented; future Kubernetes behavior is marked future.

## Capability semantic sufficiency acceptance

Before v0.4 closes, verify that the portable capability model distinguishes a provider that merely advertises the same capability identifier from a provider that is actually compatible with the application's required semantics.

Use representative existing capability families such as SQL, cache/key-value and S3 object storage.

The acceptance review must answer:

1. Can an application express a genuinely required protocol/feature semantic without naming a concrete provider product?
2. Can a provider declare the semantic subset it supports?
3. Can planning/conformance reject an incompatible provider before mutation?
4. Can BaseHarbor keep capability feature compatibility separate from availability/topology guarantees?
5. Does normal application intent stay sparse when only the capability's default/common semantics are required?

A failure here blocks the v0.5 freeze.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Normal application intent remains sparse when no non-default feature requirement exists.

- [ ] Incompatible providers are rejected before mutation.

- [ ] Representative capability specs prove semantic compatibility beyond capability-name matching.

- [ ] Representative Compose application completes the full lifecycle end to end.
- [ ] CLI/JSON/MCP expose the same semantic truth.
- [ ] A generic MCP client can discover and exercise the supported semantic surface.
- [ ] Capability-provider implementation/placement changes do not rewrite portable application intent.
- [ ] Every important state field can be classified as portable, deployment/operator, runtime, provider or protected/generated state.
- [ ] Compose project/port/network/override details are confirmed as runtime-only realization.
- [ ] No Kubernetes/OpenShift resource primitive exists in portable application intent.
- [ ] Status/doctor/policy/evidence agree.
- [ ] Backup/restore and repair/destroy remain ownership-safe.
- [ ] Exact-head acceptance evidence is captured economically.
- [ ] Optional ecosystem work remains deferred.
- [ ] No domain/lifecycle behavior exists only in CLI rendering.
- [ ] Release blockers for the v0.5 freeze are explicit.

Parent roadmap: #155
Agent interface: #215
Lifecycle semantics: #172


Depends on: #211, #172, #212, #210, #363, #483, #516, #519, #375

## Delivery boundary acceptance

Before the v0.5 freeze, BaseHarbor must classify delivery/reconciliation ownership separately from runtime and capability-provider selection.

The acceptance model must distinguish:

```text
Runtime Provider
Capability Provider
Delivery Provider
```

and prove:

- direct delivery does not become a universal architectural assumption;
- delegated delivery can exist without changing portable application intent;
- reconciliation ownership is explicit and singular;
- delivery selection/placement belongs to deployment/operator state;
- Compose remains the complete first-class direct reference path;
- future GitOps providers do not require product fields in portable intent.


## Pre-freeze architecture checklist

Before v0.4 closes, perform one explicit architecture review across the cross-cutting boundaries below. These are contract/security checks, not additional product integrations or new release tracks.

### Identity boundary

- [ ] Application identity and BaseHarbor operator identity remain separate.
- [ ] Managed application identity from #363 fits the existing capability/provider/lifecycle model.
- [ ] Identity-provider realization does not leak Keycloak-specific concepts into portable application intent.
- [ ] Workload/machine identity, human identity and provider-admin credentials remain distinct.

### Secrets and credential boundary

- [ ] Human end-user credentials remain owned by the identity provider and are not mirrored into OpenBao.
- [ ] Machine/provider secrets use secure bindings and protected/generated state.
- [ ] Long-lived unrestricted provider-admin credentials are not exposed to applications.
- [ ] Rotation/revocation can occur without rewriting portable application intent.

### Network and connectivity boundary

- [ ] Portable semantics can express required connectivity direction and exposure intent without runtime-specific networking fields.
- [ ] Public/private/internal exposure remains deployment/provider realization rather than product-specific application configuration.
- [ ] Deny-by-default relationships and explicit required connectivity remain enforceable.
- [ ] Future Kubernetes NetworkPolicy, service-mesh, VPC/subnet and firewall realization can fit without changing portable intent.

### PKI and certificate lifecycle

- [ ] Certificates, private keys and trust material are protected/generated state or external references, never ordinary portable application data.
- [ ] Ownership of CA/trust anchors and issued certificates is explicit.
- [ ] Expiry/invalid trust is observable and actionable.
- [ ] Rotation/reissuance can reconcile safely.
- [ ] mTLS requirements can be expressed provider/runtime-neutrally without embedding a specific PKI product.

### Backup and restore semantics

- [ ] Backup success requires verification, not only artifact creation.
- [ ] Restore includes compatibility preflight, data/state restoration, rebind/reconcile and semantic verification.
- [ ] Provider-owned data backup remains the responsibility of the provider that understands its data semantics.
- [ ] Ownership and foreign/platform-managed resources remain safe during restore/recovery.
- [ ] Backup/restore metadata is sufficient for later version/runtime compatibility handling.

### Artifact and software-supply-chain boundary

- [ ] Runtime/provider artifacts have deterministic identities where practical, including digest/version identity.
- [ ] Artifact provenance/signature/SBOM evidence can be attached or verified later without changing portable application intent.
- [ ] Production policy can reject ambiguous or unverifiable artifacts without product-specific fields in the app contract.
- [ ] Registry/distribution location remains deployment/operator/runtime concern, consistent with #181.
- [ ] No pre-v0.5 requirement is created to implement a specific signing, SBOM or registry product.

### Audit, evidence and ownership

- [ ] Security-sensitive lifecycle decisions produce secret-safe evidence.
- [ ] Ownership is explicit across application, shared, external/platform and protected/generated state.
- [ ] Audit/evidence can identify the effective policy, actor/workload identity, provider/runtime and verified outcome without storing secret material.
- [ ] Drift/repair/destroy remain ownership-safe across every reviewed boundary.

### Interface parity

- [ ] CLI, JSON and MCP expose the same semantic truth for the reviewed boundaries.
- [ ] No required lifecycle/security behavior exists only in CLI presentation code.
- [ ] Unsupported/unverifiable/denied/conflict/foreign-owned/degraded results remain typed and machine-readable.

Any failed item that requires a new portable primitive blocks the v0.5 freeze. Product-specific convenience, admin UIs and optional integrations do not.


## Pre-release gate

Before creating this release:

- [ ] All acceptance criteria in this issue are complete.
- [ ] Required local/repository tests pass.
- [ ] The full relevant CI matrix has passed at least once on the **exact release-candidate commit**.
- [ ] Docker and Podman acceptance pass where applicable.
- [ ] Security, isolation and secret-leak checks pass where applicable.
- [ ] The documentation audit defined by #364 passes.
- [ ] Human-facing documentation matches the shipped behavior.
- [ ] Reference and normative specs match every changed public contract.
- [ ] No unresolved release blocker remains.
- [ ] Version, changelog, release notes and release metadata are consistent.
- [ ] Final exact-head acceptance evidence is recorded before tagging/releasing.

Acceptance answers whether the feature/release scope is complete. This gate answers whether the exact commit is safe and documented well enough to release.

Do not weaken or skip a required check merely to complete the release. Checks that are genuinely not applicable should be recorded as such rather than silently omitted.


## Standards-first extensible runtime-provider acceptance

Runtime-boundary acceptance depends on #396.

Before this issue can close:

- Docker and Podman must exercise the same provider-neutral runtime boundary intended for future third-party runtimes.
- Portable/core orchestration must not require direct `bhruntime.Compose` coupling.
- Product-specific runtime branching must remain behind provider implementations.
- Runtime semantics must reuse existing open/de-facto standards wherever applicable; any BaseHarbor-specific semantic must be justified by a documented standards gap from #390/#396.
- Adding a conforming future runtime must not require changes to portable application intent.
- Compose remains a first-class supported standard/source/realization mechanism, but not the identity of the BaseHarbor runtime abstraction.

Depends on: #396


## Target boundary acceptance

The Target model is already defined and implemented by **#408 / v0.4.15**. This issue does not redesign it.

v0.4.21 must only prove that the completed runtime/capability/delivery boundaries preserve and correctly consume the frozen Target semantics:

```text
Target
├── Runtime Provider
├── Access Reference
└── Scope

Deployment identity
= Target + Application + Environment
```

Acceptance:

- [ ] Runtime, Capability and Delivery Provider work does not introduce a second Target/Context model.
- [ ] Runtime Provider selection is consumed from the resolved Target rather than portable application intent.
- [ ] Access Reference and Scope remain deployment/operator state established by #408.
- [ ] Multiple Targets and multiple deployments remain isolated through the #408 Target-scoped state model.
- [ ] CLI, JSON and MCP continue to expose the same effective Target/deployment identity.
- [ ] Portable application intent remains unchanged when the Target changes.
- [ ] Runtime/provider refactors preserve #408 ownership and fail-closed Target semantics.

## MCP / machine-interface parity gate

This release changes BaseHarbor semantics and therefore MUST update the machine/agent surface in the same release.

Hard rule:

```text
new or changed BaseHarbor semantic
        ↓
shared domain/lifecycle core
        ↓
CLI + JSON + MCP updated together
```

Requirements:

- MCP/JSON MUST expose the new or changed semantic wherever it is useful to an agent or automation;
- MCP MUST reuse the same shared core as the human CLI and MUST NOT wrap CLI subprocesses;
- no shell, Docker, Compose, Podman or provider-native escape hatch may be introduced;
- read-only, mutating and destructive safety classifications remain explicit;
- policy, ownership, preflight, reconciliation, verification, confirmation and secret-safety semantics MUST remain identical across human and agent paths;
- unsupported agent operations fail explicitly with typed actionable results;
- documentation, machine discovery and generic MCP-client acceptance are updated in the same release;
- the MCP surface remains small and semantic rather than mirroring every CLI command 1:1.

This is a release gate, not follow-up work for a later version.


## Stable identity prerequisite

- #483 — stable application and deployment identity

The v0.4.21 acceptance must not close until stable application/deployment identity is resolved so v0.5 freezes durable technical identity rather than mutable names.


## Workload source / repository adoption acceptance

Depends on: #519

Before v0.4 closes, prove that repository workload-source representation is not confused with Runtime or Delivery Provider semantics.

Acceptance:

- [ ] Compose, Quadlet, Kubernetes manifests, Kustomize and Helm are classified as repository workload sources/adoption inputs, not portable runtime identities.
- [ ] The portable Application Contract does not require source kind/path.
- [ ] Existing workload.compose compatibility is preserved without freezing Compose as canonical workload identity.
- [ ] Logical workload component identity remains stable across source-native representations.
- [ ] Repository source metadata is separated from portable application intent, Target state and runtime/provider state.
- [ ] app inspect/init use the same normalized evidence semantics across supported source adapters.
- [ ] Understanding a Kubernetes/Helm/Kustomize repository does not imply runtime support or ownership of live Kubernetes resources.
- [ ] Runtime Provider and Delivery Provider compatibility is checked after source inspection/adoption through typed plan/preflight results.
- [ ] CLI/JSON/MCP expose the same source-neutral repository semantics.


## Actionable diagnostics / no-dead-end-error acceptance

Depends on: #375

BaseHarbor's semantic acceptance includes the rule:

> **Wenn BaseHarbor Nein sagt, muss BaseHarbor auch sagen warum und wie es weitergeht.**

Canonical engineering form:

```text
No dead-end errors.
```

Before this issue can close:

- [ ] known failures use one shared typed diagnostic/problem model below presentation layers;
- [ ] CLI, JSON and MCP expose the same cause/remediation semantics;
- [ ] fail-closed outcomes explain both the reason and the safe path forward;
- [ ] unsupported, invalid, denied, unverifiable and foreign-owned results remain distinguishable;
- [ ] known recoverable failures offer/propose safe repair where BaseHarbor can do so deterministically;
- [ ] every known unrecoverable failure provides the next useful action;
- [ ] raw provider/runtime errors are diagnostic detail, not the primary human message;
- [ ] Plan, Preflight, Doctor and lifecycle commands do not maintain competing error taxonomies;
- [ ] tests protect semantic problem fields and secret-safe rendering.

A v0.5 freeze is not complete if failure semantics still exist only as arbitrary error strings.


## Capability-subset acceptance dependency

- #553 — reference demo config-matrix must prove valid capability subsets, mixed combinations and invalid cross-capability contracts.

The full-feature demo is not sufficient evidence that reduced Application Contracts converge correctly.


## Final pre-acceptance dependencies

Semantic acceptance MUST NOT begin until these focused pre-freeze releases are complete:

- #569 — v0.4.21 Application-to-Application Consumption Contract
- #570 — v0.4.22 MCP Operator Authorization and Extension Trust
- #571 — v0.4.23 Freeze Readiness Policy, Public Namespace and Platform Contract

Depends on: #569, #570, #571, #603


## CLI consolidation dependency

Semantic acceptance MUST use the final human CLI surface established by #603 rather than validating an intermediate command structure.

- #603 — v0.4.24 Human CLI surface consolidation

The acceptance review must prove that CLI simplification did not create a second lifecycle or diverge from JSON/MCP semantics.


## Pre-freeze compatibility rule

BaseHarbor is still pre-freeze.

Hard rule:

```text
before v0.5 freeze
    ->
no legacy compatibility requirement
no migration requirement
no compatibility aliases required
no preservation of obsolete pre-freeze behavior
```

If an existing pre-freeze design, command, schema, state layout, file format, naming convention or behavior is wrong or no longer fits the target architecture, replace it with the correct model instead of carrying compatibility baggage forward.

Do NOT add:

- legacy modes;
- migration layers for pre-freeze-only state;
- deprecated compatibility paths;
- alias preservation solely for historical pre-freeze behavior;
- duplicate old/new documentation trees;
- compatibility shims for interfaces that are not yet frozen.

The priority before v0.5 is to converge on the correct final contract and UX.

Compatibility and migration guarantees begin only once the relevant contract is intentionally frozen/versioned in v0.5.x.


---

## Release umbrella / child issues

This issue is the **release-level umbrella**. It owns scope, ordering, cross-cutting acceptance and release completion.

Implementation work SHOULD live in focused child issues. Child issues MUST reference this release issue as their parent. Do not keep expanding the release issue with implementation-detail checklists when a focused child issue is clearer.

Focused child issues should be created as implementation slices become concrete. Do not create tickets merely to mirror headings; split only independently implementable/testable work.

Closing the release umbrella requires all required child issues plus cross-cutting release/documentation/validation acceptance to be complete.


## Developer access and credential portability dependency

Semantic acceptance also depends on #777 — developer access, credential portability and profile export/import.

Before #174 can close, #777 must prove the standards-first access model: no mandatory BaseHarbor login for ordinary local development; native Git/SSH/kubeconfig/cloud authentication first; minimal temporary-vs-secure credential UX; secure credentials remain protected and recoverable; developer profile export/import remains distinct from application backup/restore; remote target secrets are not silently replicated to developer machines.

Depends on: #777


## Independent developer validation

Before v0.4 closes, at least one developer who did not implement the tested feature/path must complete the public reference journey from the shipped documentation without undocumented assistance.

This is a product/DX acceptance check, not a broad beta program.

The validation should start from a clean or realistically independent developer setup and use the same public documentation and normal CLI that a new user receives.

Capture at minimum:

- time to first successful application run;
- unclear or unnecessary prompts;
- undocumented prerequisites or manual workarounds;
- dead-end errors or missing next actions;
- terminology/navigation confusion;
- authentication/onboarding friction;
- any point where implementation knowledge was required.

Hard rule:

```text
If a normal developer cannot complete the documented happy path
without private implementation knowledge,
the v0.4 semantic/DX acceptance is not complete.
```

Findings that reveal correctness, security, documentation or normal-path DX gaps block acceptance until resolved or explicitly reclassified with a justified non-blocking scope.

### Additional acceptance

- [ ] At least one independent developer completes the documented Dev Local reference journey.
- [ ] Where Dev Remote is part of the shipped v0.4.25 acceptance scope, at least one independent developer completes its documented onboarding/import happy path.
- [ ] No undocumented implementation knowledge is required.
- [ ] Any required workaround is either removed or documented as an explicit supported step before acceptance.
- [ ] Findings and resolution are linked as release evidence before #174 closes.


## Core definition acceptance

Before the v0.5 freeze, verify one consistent product definition across CLI, Console, docs and machine contracts:

```text
BaseHarbor Core = SQL + Secrets + Identity
```

Acceptance must also prove that mandatory capability does not imply mandatory shared placement: the same provider-neutral semantics support shared placement and application-isolated placement without changing portable application intent or creating a second lifecycle.


## Host-platform portability acceptance child

- [ ] #817 — prove that the final pre-freeze semantics do not encode Linux-only host assumptions and that WSL2/macOS can be added after freeze without reopening portable/runtime/provider contracts.


## Kubernetes pre-freeze architecture-proof decision

The existing draft PR #616 — **Kubernetes pre-freeze adoption contract and architecture proof** — must be explicitly resolved before this semantic-acceptance release closes.

#616 is not a Kubernetes support release. Its purpose is narrower and directly relevant to the freeze question:

> Can Kubernetes consume the final BaseHarbor semantics without requiring new Application, Capability, Identity, Policy or user-facing Core contracts?

Before #174 closes:

- rebase or otherwise evaluate #616 against the final v0.4.25 contract/head rather than relying on its September baseline;
- validate that the same portable Application Intent can be consumed by the Kubernetes proof without Kubernetes-specific fields;
- validate Target/namespace separation, stable identity, runtime-neutral capability/binding semantics, ownership-safe destroy and namespace-scoped operation;
- validate that READY/status/doctor/evidence and CLI/JSON/MCP semantics do not need a Kubernetes-specific Core fork;
- review any gaps discovered by the proof and fix genuine missing portable primitives before freeze;
- make an explicit final decision: accept the proof as sufficient architecture/portability evidence, supersede it with equivalent current-head evidence, or reject it with documented rationale.

Hard rule:

```text
open/forgotten draft != portability evidence
```

No production Kubernetes hardening, full storage/HA/Gateway parity, Operator/CRDs or OpenShift support is required here unless the proof demonstrates that a missing semantic contract would otherwise be frozen incorrectly.

Additional acceptance:

- [ ] #616 is explicitly evaluated against the final v0.4.25 semantic surface;
- [ ] its portability findings are either accepted, superseded by equivalent proof, or rejected with rationale;
- [ ] no unresolved Kubernetes-discovered contract gap remains before v0.5 freeze;
- [ ] architecture-proof success is not documented as production Kubernetes support.


## Console AI assistant pre-freeze boundary

A future built-in AI assistant in the BaseHarbor Console must fit the frozen machine/MCP model without creating a new control plane or direct runtime path.

Target architecture:

```text
Console AI assistant
        ↓
BaseHarbor MCP / Machine Contract
        ↓
BaseHarbor Core
        ↓
Policy / Authorization / Approval
        ↓
Target Access
```

Pre-freeze acceptance only:

- [ ] an AI assistant is classified as a client of the existing Machine/MCP surface, not a new authority;
- [ ] it cannot call Docker, Podman, Kubernetes, OpenShift or the Node Connector directly;
- [ ] read-only discovery/planning can reuse existing machine safety metadata;
- [ ] mutating/destructive operations remain subject to the same authorization, policy, confirmation and approval semantics as every other client;
- [ ] AI/provider endpoint configuration is Console/platform configuration, not portable Application Intent;
- [ ] model/provider choice remains replaceable and does not enter BaseHarbor domain contracts;
- [ ] AI credentials are handled through the existing protected secret/credential boundary and are not persisted as ordinary browser-local state;
- [ ] no new BaseHarbor lifecycle or tool semantics are introduced only for AI.

Explicit non-goals for v0.4.25:

- no built-in chat/assistant implementation requirement;
- no OpenAI/Ollama/Anthropic/provider integration requirement;
- no model-hosting requirement;
- no new AI-specific Core service;
- no AI-specific bypass around MCP/Machine authorization.

Freeze rule:

Passing this check means a later Console AI assistant can be added after v0.5 without reopening the frozen BaseHarbor semantic model.


## v0.4.24 integration handoff: acceptance delta for v0.4.25 (2026-10-09)

The v0.4.25 acceptance baseline is **the released, runtime-evidenced v0.4.24 contract**, not an intermediate pre-release branch or a prior CLI tree. Tracking: Core/HA #837; etcd-DCS recovery #847; provider upgrades #845/#848; CLI/Node/docs #846; integration/QA #849. The QA candidate `8cf91e25cf80c8831acb833500cf0bbcc27ae64b` has green static Go gates but is **not** evidence of successful runtime upgrade, HA failover, durable restore, or v0.4.24 release acceptance.

The following are **cross-cutting acceptance tests**, not permission to duplicate v0.4.24 implementation in this release:

- [ ] **Core and Target separation:** `baha use`/Target selection, the selected management Core, Dev Local vs Dev Remote, and application deployment Target remain separate concepts. Validate 0/1/N registered Cores/Targets, persisted selection, explicit-Target precedence, and CLI/JSON/MCP semantic consistency. Target/Access is operator state; no second Target or Core model.
- [ ] **Canonical human commands:** Validate the shipped `baha app sql`, `baha app cache`, `baha node add/connect/list/status/disconnect`, and task-oriented wizard flows from #603/#846 against machine contracts. No pre-freeze alias is retained solely for backwards compatibility (no `app psql`/`app valkey` resurrection).
- [ ] **Managed-provider lifecycle truth:** Core SQL + Secrets + Identity must maintain explicit ownership, shared vs isolated placement, independently verifiable installed and desired version/digest, and read-only plan vs mutating execute boundaries. Unsupported/foreign or unverifiable provider versions must fail before mutation with typed reason and next action.
- [ ] **HA/DCS recovery semantics:** Test the shipped `ha: false` and `ha: true` configurations, authenticated etcd cluster/member identity and mTLS, immutable etcd snapshot evidence, isolated restore, DCS quorum/rejoin, Patroni leader/replica readiness and rolling upgrade/resume. A backup receipt or file-only restore is not recovered-service evidence. Recovery must never overwrite foreign/existing etcd data or touch unrelated installations.
- [ ] **Provider-specific recovery:** Test a real supported version delta and partial-failure recovery for PostgreSQL/Spilo, OpenBao (AppRole/policies/application secrets) and Keycloak (SQL-backed realms, discovery, OIDC/token flow). Preserve protected material, verify post-recovery semantics, and distinguish provider-specific backup from Core state/credential-profile export.
- [ ] **Remote Node and Console:** Check one-use scoped enrollment, mTLS renewal/revocation, delegated Target authorization, and one-Core-to-multiple-Targets Console visibility. No direct Console/AI/agent control of Node Connector or provider runtime; all mutations use existing Core policy/approval/audit semantics.
- [ ] **Same-SHA release evidence:** Complete final v0.4.24 Docker/Podman and relevant HA/provider/remote-gate results on a pinned release SHA, then carry confirmed behavior into v0.4.25 documentation, independent developer journeys and the exact-head v0.4.25 matrix. Static HF tests alone do not close these items.

Scope rule: defects inherited from v0.4.24 must be corrected against their owning feature/release before claiming the v0.4.25 baseline. v0.4.25 does not create another updater, another HA controller, or another credential/identity model.


## v0.4.25 mandatory desktop developer-platform delivery (2026-10-09)

**Release decision:** Full supported developer workflows on macOS and Windows through WSL2 are in scope **before the v0.5 freeze**. The former architecture-only interpretation of #817 is superseded. Implementation parent #818 and children #819–#823 are mandatory v0.4.25 dependencies.

**Supported topology (not native Windows containers):**
- macOS: native `baha` for Darwin arm64 and amd64, Docker Desktop and/or Podman Machine as verified Linux-container runtimes.
- Windows: `baha` running in actual WSL2 Linux, Docker Desktop WSL integration and/or WSL2-local Linux Docker/Podman as independently verified. Native Windows CLI/runtime support may be delivered separately, but is **not** a prerequisite for a complete WSL2 journey.
- Linux: existing Docker and rootless Podman remain regression-protected. Dev Remote to existing Core/Target must remain available across host platforms.

**Release-blocking acceptance:**
- [ ] #819/#820 complete minimal Host Platform Contract and Linux migration with no regression.
- [ ] #821 completes real WSL2 install, discovery, effective VM capacity, trust/browser boundary, Dev Local and Dev Remote journeys on a genuine WSL2 machine.
- [ ] #822 completes Darwin native installer/update, trust/keychain and secure file handling, ARM64/amd64 conformance, and real Docker Desktop / Podman Machine workflow where declared supported.
- [ ] #823 records native and **actual runtime** platform evidence. Cross-compilation and unit tests alone cannot qualify a platform as SUPPORTED.
- [ ] On both macOS and WSL2, a developer can install `baha`, initialize/adopt a representative repository, use Core/Target selection, run plan/up/status/doctor/logs, access `app sql/cache`, and cleanly destroy their **owned** dev deployment using supported runtime integration.
- [ ] Test Developer Remote enrollment/import, reconnect, scoped mTLS and offboarding on both hosts, with no duplicate Target/Core model or secret leakage.
- [ ] Negative tests cover unavailable Docker/Podman VM, insufficient effective VM memory, missing trust, denied permissions, broken network, unsupported systemd/Quadlet path, and unsafe cleanup with actionable errors.
- [ ] EN/DE getting started and platform support matrix explicitly identify verified runtime combinations and any excluded features; one independent developer on macOS and one on Windows/WSL2 complete a public-docs happy path.
- [ ] The final v0.4.25 release candidate carries exact-head OS-specific build/unit/conformance **and** targeted disposable runtime-gate evidence before tagging.

**Scope control:** Do not create a second Core, lifecycle engine, Runtime Provider or proprietary host plugin framework. Native Windows executable/container support and every possible Docker/Podman/architecture combination are not required. Claim SUPPORT only for combinations proven by real execution. Resolve actual usability blockers before freeze rather than downgrading the whole macOS/WSL2 goal to an architecture audit.


## Three parallel development sessions — v0.4.25 execution plan

All three sessions work on separate branches and PRs. The common integration branch belongs to Session 3. Changes to shared interfaces are coordinated through explicit handoffs.

### Session 1 — Host Platform Contract, Linux and macOS
Issues: #819, #820, #822 (parent #818).

- Implement the minimal shared Host Platform Contract first and provide its API to Session 2.
- Implement Linux adapters and regression tests.
- Implement native macOS/Darwin support for arm64/amd64, filesystem, trust, effective runtime capacity, install/update and developer workflows with supported Docker Desktop / Podman Machine integrations.
- Own shared host interfaces and Linux/Darwin implementation files. Do not edit Session 2 developer-access or WSL2 implementations.

### Session 2 — Windows/WSL2 and Developer Access
Issues: #821, #777.

- Implement real WSL2 developer workflows, host/runtime classification, effective VM resources, filesystem and trust boundaries, and supported Docker/Podman integration.
- Implement Dev Local/Remote onboarding, management-Core selection/import, credential/profile export/import, enrollment and offboarding.
- Consume Session 1's Host Platform API; do not create a second abstraction.
- Own WSL2-specific and developer-access implementation files. Do not edit Linux/Darwin adapters.

### Session 3 — Integration, semantic acceptance and QA
Issues: #823, #817, #174.

- Own the common integration branch, shared CLI registration, dependency-file integration, CI workflows, EN/DE documentation and support matrix.
- Integrate Sessions 1 and 2 incrementally and resolve conflicts without overwriting actively owned implementation.
- Check CLI/JSON/MCP parity, security/ownership contracts, Linux regressions and real macOS/WSL2 developer journeys.
- Record final acceptance on one exact integration SHA.

### Tests and execution permission

- **Use Hugging Face for fast tests.**
- **All three sessions are explicitly authorized to use GitHub Actions when necessary** for macOS, WSL2, Docker/Podman, platform-specific and release-relevant tests.
- Prefer targeted tests first; perform the full relevant matrix on the final integration SHA.
- Runtime support is only accepted with real runtime evidence. Do not start a pre-release, merge or tag until the v0.4.25 acceptance gates are complete.


---

## v0.4.25 binding addition — Capability-first, core-less applications and minimal footprint (2026-10-10)

### Product contract
**Declare what you need. Run only what you need.** Capability requirements are the sole application-intent truth. Infrastructure footprint is an **derived, observable projection**, not a security level, independent profile, policy override or second configuration model. No `security.profile`, `custom` level or artificial linear hierarchy. HTTPS, identity, SQL, cache and managed secrets are orthogonal; a web app can require HTTPS without Keycloak, or identity without a public gateway.

- A valid application with zero managed capabilities MUST run on a fresh supported runtime (Docker or Podman) using the `baha` CLI **without installing or starting any BaseHarbor Core container or requiring BaseHarbor login**. No implicit SQL or Core dependency.
- Sparse requests such as `sql: true`, `secrets: true`, `identity: true`, `https: true` and empty `{}` are the **target authoring shorthand**. Shorthand is an authoring projection only: it MUST normalize into the **one canonical versioned application contract**; no independent shorthand database/state, divergent parser semantics or duplicate contract authority. Keep an author-owned shorthand file editable; never silently rewrite developer-authored source.
- Stable application identity is generated **once** during initialization and durably stored in the existing authoritative owner/state location; subsequent reads reuse it. Absent, mismatched or duplicated identity MUST be diagnosed/fail closed instead of generating a new ID on every invocation. Explicitly pin and test the state owner and regeneration behavior.
- Remove the existing `application.New()` implicit SQL fallback. A wizard suggestion is permitted only when clearly visible and opt-out; a canonical contract NEVER silently adds unrequested capabilities.
- A versioned **capability -> required services/dependencies** resolution policy uses the existing Target, provider registry, installation ownership and deployment registry. Provider selection can reuse existing external/BYO/shared capabilities; do not assume `sql` always requires a new PostgreSQL container or `secrets` a new isolated OpenBao stack. Resolve **the union of active application requirements per installation/Target**, plus existing owned state; never silently stop a service because one app drops a requirement.
- Footprint is a read-only machine evidence projection (proposed `baseharbor.footprint/v1`) showing demanded capabilities, selected service dependencies, why they are required, new versus reused containers and additional memory. Distinguish measured, estimated and unknown; never invent counts or RAM. CLI `baha app footprint show` and plan/JSON/MCP share one resolver and evidence semantics.
- The footprint resolver MUST CONSUME existing authoritative installation/Target/deployment/runtime/provider state. It MUST NOT become a second state registry, lifecycle manager or implicit fixer. Regressions specifically cross-check #828, #865 and #868 state-boundary classes: exists != running, single canonical state directory/owner, and safe post-destroy rebootstrap.
- Unused owned shared-Core services are **visible drift/idle footprint, not desired permanent overhead**. Provide an explicit, confirmed, ownership-safe reclaim/retirement action later; removal is NEVER silent and MUST preserve foreign/other-app data and resources. Resolve and prove the semantic distinction before freeze even when resource reclamation implementation is deferred.
- Explicit app-owned security decisions remain developer-controlled; BaseHarbor's own invariant protection, cross-app isolation and external operator policy remain intact. No new Security Levels.

### Greenfield and change UX
- `baha app new` uses a compact **single-screen TUI multi-select checklist** (space toggles, arrows navigate): SQL, cache, managed secrets, identity/login, public HTTPS; additional capabilities progressively disclosed. An empty selection is valid. Detection may preselect visibly, never impose silent mandatory services.
- After selection display **at most a few lines**: resolved required services, new/reused container count, *incremental* RAM estimate and evidence quality; optional detail on demand. Confirmation `Yes` enters normal plan -> preflight -> apply -> verify. `No` returns to the **same checklist with all selections retained**, repeat indefinitely. Cancel is no mutation.
- Re-edit via proposed `baha app edit` or manual contract change is available throughout the lifecycle. `app edit` is a mutating operation: show exact intent diff and impact, require explicit confirmation; in `--no-input` / EOF / non-TTY never silently accept defaults or write. Manual contract edits are respected, and `app up` reconciles the diff with the existing safety contract.
- No dead ends, default-short help, no credential/provider internals during the happy path, no repetitive yes/no interrogation. CLI/JSON/MCP/GUI expose the same semantics (machine mutation has typed authorization/confirmation contract without artificial TTY).
- Reserve proposed names `baha app edit` and `baha app footprint show` as v0.4.25 interfaces; do **not** destabilize the in-progress v0.4.24 pre-release or claim these exist in 0.4.24.

### Integration sequencing / three parallel sessions
**Gate 0: released and runtime-proven v0.4.24 baseline**; no 0.4.25 changes into v0.4.24 pre-release.

**Session 1 — Contract + Footprint/Standalone runtime (new focused child):**
1. Freeze shortest shorthand/canonical/identity semantics, zero-capability legality, provider/Target dependency rules and footprint v1 contract.
2. Implement no-implicit-SQL, one canonical normalization path, central resolver/read-only footprint, core-less path and registry/ownership-safe planning.
3. Pure Go contract/state negative tests first; target-specific Docker/Podman gates after integration. Own `internal/application`, dedicated resolver/domain packages and Core plan/runtime seams. **Do not edit** wizard/TUI, host adapters or platform CI.
4. Publish stable contract interface/fixtures for Sessions 2/3 immediately, without waiting for full runtime implementation.

**Session 2 — Developer UX, CLI/JSON/MCP (new focused child; align #777):**
1. After the Session 1 contract fixture is pinned, implement the compact multi-select new/edit TUI, preview -> confirm/no -> retained-selection loop, sparse contract UX, help/non-TTY safety.
2. Expose footprint show and consistent plan/JSON/MCP machine contracts by calling **Session 1 resolver**, never duplicating capability/dependency/footprint logic.
3. Own `cmd/baha` wizard/presentation/command registration, TUI rendering, public machine-surface adapters and EN/DE UX pages. **Do not edit** application/core resolver or host-adapter internals.
4. Coordinate ownership with #777 access/import to avoid two sessions touching the same CLI files; #777 access work is sequenced behind common CLI integration or confined to different paths.

**Session 3 — Host-platform + real qualification (existing #818, #819–#823):**
1. #819 minimal Host Platform Contract and architecture guard, then #820 Linux adapter baseline, #821 WSL2, #822 Darwin in parallel **only after #819 is stable**; #823 cross-platform evidence last.
2. Own `internal/host* `/OS-specific adapters and related platform conformance/CI. Avoid edits to Session 1 resolver or Session 2 wizard files; negotiate any shared `cmd/baha` glue explicitly through Session 2.
3. Qualify real macOS and actual WSL2 developer journeys (not just cross-compilation). Use appropriate GitHub Actions when required and fast targeted Hugging Face checks where applicable. No unsupported platform claim.
4. Consume core-less standalone and UX contract fixtures once available; run full end-to-end platform UX only on merged integration candidate.

**Final integration / acceptance under #174 (after all three):**
- One pinned shared candidate SHA; merge changes in dependency order: Session 1 canonical semantics -> Session 2 UX/machine surfaces -> Session 3 platform integration; independent #777/#862 QA tracks respect file ownership.
- Fast atomic checks first; rerun only missing/failed gates. Then Docker + rootless Podman, fresh no-Core app, shared provider union/reuse, add/remove/reconcile, partial/foreign state, #828/#865/#868, failure/rollback and CLI/JSON/MCP parity; native Darwin/real WSL2 #823. Exact-SHA evidence and EN/DE docs; no pre-release before all gates.
- Do not claim Core footprint optimization is complete merely because core-less apps work: full on-demand Identity, selective Compose/Quadlet and explicit orphan-service reclaim may be postponed **only with an accurate support/acceptance scope**. The v0.5 freeze must not falsely promise unimplemented behavior.

### Additive acceptance
- [ ] Canonical contract, shorthand normalization and stable-ID owner verified; no second state truth.
- [ ] Empty capability application starts fresh without Core; no implicit SQL and no login.
- [ ] Shared/external provider reuse and Target union are deterministic, ownership-safe and observable.
- [ ] Footprint v1 is read-only, source-attributed and consistent across plan/CLI/JSON/MCP; memory evidence classified.
- [ ] New/edit TUI checklist, compact preview, No-back-loop, cancel/EOF/non-TTY and no-dead-end cases proven.
- [ ] Dynamic add/remove and existing lifecycle, confirmation, preservation and idempotency proven.
- [ ] State boundary regressions #828/#865/#868 covered without inventing new state owners.
- [ ] #777 and #818–#823 remain aligned with no competing CLI/host ownership.
- [ ] Real Docker/Podman/macOS/WSL2 and exact candidate SHA evidence meet respective support claims.


## Verbindlicher PR-Workflow: ein gemeinsamer Release-PR, zwei Sessions (2026-10-10)

- **Genau ein gemeinsamer Entwicklungs-/Integrations-PR pro Release** gegen `release/v0.4.xx`; keine zwei parallelen Session-PRs.
- Beide Sessions arbeiten **direkt in diesem einen PR** auf demselben Feature-/Integrationsbranch und pushen ihre abgegrenzten Commits dorthin. Keine getrennten Session-PRs als Standard.
- Vor jeder Änderung aktuellen Branch-HEAD prüfen, eigene Dateigrenzen einhalten, bei gemeinsamen Dateien abstimmen; niemals fremde Commits überschreiben oder Force-Push. Häufig synchronisieren und gezielte Tests nach Änderungen ausführen.
- Die Sessions können parallel arbeiten, jedoch geteilte Schnittstellen zuerst abstimmen. Gemeinsamer PR zeigt jederzeit den tatsächlich integrierten Stand.
- Ein gemeinsamer finaler SHA, gezielte Gates vor teuren Runtime-Gates, anschließend Pre-Release und Release nach gesonderter Freigabe.
- **Diese Regel ersetzt jede ältere Angabe zu „zwei PRs“, „separaten Arbeitsbranches/PRs“ oder Session-3-Integrationsbranches in dieser Issue-Planung.**

## v0.4.18 completion clarification

This issue is the **pre-freeze acceptance gate**, not the place to defer known correctness/DX gaps into v0.5.

Before #174 can close, the current v0.4 implementation must prove:

- READY means desired == realized == verified for supported runtime/workload artifacts.
- stale/incompatible BaseHarbor runtime artifacts cannot report READY (#367).
- stale repository `build:` artifacts cannot survive a successful convergence after source changes (#379).
- artifact/image identity is represented behind the existing Desired/Observed/Diff/Ownership/Reconcile/Verify model rather than by a parallel image-specific lifecycle.
- Docker and Podman expose the same semantic result despite Compose vs Quadlet realization.
- application intent stays capability-oriented (e.g. logical SQL); PostgreSQL is a current/default provider realization, not portable intent.
- provider/product/version/artifact realization is transparent in diagnostics/machine state without forcing it into portable intent.
- the guided developer path from #368–#375 works coherently and #372 proves it from a pristine repository.
- deterministic CI remains separately available from the interactive/guided journey.

#174 should therefore consume the concrete results of #367–#379 and classify any remaining ambiguity as a blocker for #175.
